note: One controlled case per declared refusal, plus a positive case that must earn none. Each defeating case must earn EXACTLY the code it names: a case that fires for a second reason has not proved the one it is for, and two refusals that cannot be separated are one rule wearing two names. The lines and crosswalk entries are the oracle's own; no case reads STATUS.yaml, so a repair to the live file cannot quietly stop a refusal from being proved. The positive case must type a real entry - an empty document against an empty crosswalk satisfies every rule and proves nothing.
revision_note: v3 answers a second independent observation against 964f414 (reports/observations/2026-08-27-status-claims-second-witness-observation.json). v2's standing rule compared a token and treated a preceding NOT as denial; the witness walked past it with NOT_YET_WITNESSED, NEVER_WITNESSED, AWAITING_WITNESSED and BUILT-NOT_WITNESSED, the last because splitting on underscores alone hides a hyphenated negator. v2's FIELD_UNREADABLE closed the two shapes v1's witness reported and not the class. Four standing refusals collapse into one biconditional here, and the negator cases below exist so the vocabulary question cannot come back.

cases.proves: A field typed with the derived subject, the kind its value's prefix admits, and the standing its value leads with earns no refusal.

A value that does not lead with a rung declares no standing, and that is the correct entry rather than a defect. PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT says the contract is built; it does not put the subject at BUILT.

crosswalk.subject: node-identity
crosswalk.detail: the proposed contract is built and its registry read slice serves

cases.proves: An entry missing a required field is refused rather than raising. A missing standing raised KeyError and a null subject raised TypeError inside sorted().

crosswalk.subject: asset-service
crosswalk.detail: an entry that never declares a standing at all

cases.proves: A status field the crosswalk does not type is a defect, so the typing cannot silently fall behind the document.

The detector catches the class, not the reported instances. A hyphenated key is invisible to the strict reader and plausible here - ai-native is repository vocabulary - and an earlier detector written against indentation and spaces could not see it.
A crosswalk entry naming a field and value the document no longer carries is a defect, so the typing cannot outlive what it types.

crosswalk.subject: retired-thing
crosswalk.detail: a claim the document has since dropped

cases.proves: The subject is derived from the field, not declared. A witness dissolved a real collision by renaming one side of it to byom-ruling; a derived subject cannot be renamed.

crosswalk.subject: byom-ruling
crosswalk.detail: a subject renamed to escape a collision

cases.proves: A kind outside the declared three is refused. A witness typo'd RULING as RULLING, which split the collision group and silently disabled the rules keyed on the kind string.

crosswalk.subject: ticket-kind-vocabulary
crosswalk.detail: a typo that would disable the rules keyed on this field

cases.proves: Two claims of one kind about one subject stay a duplicate. Typing distinguishes a status from a ruling; it does not excuse writing one subject's status twice. Two identical entries earn this too, which is why a separate duplicate-entry refusal would be the same rule twice.

crosswalk.subject: proofing-service
crosswalk.detail: a second status claim about the same subject

cases.proves: The rule is total in both directions. A witness retyped an accepted packet value as a plain status and an earlier draft admitted it, because that draft guarded only the ruling-and-acceptance pair. OWNER_ACCEPTANCE is irreversible and settled by seat:root; STATUS is neither.

crosswalk.subject: specification
crosswalk.detail: an act of the root seat demoted to a reversible status

cases.proves: The whole standing rule, and the reason it has no negation vocabulary. Every line here declares WITNESSED on a value that does not lead with it: the first is the T3 trap, and the rest are the synonyms and the hyphen a NOT-aware token comparison let through. A rule that asks what the value leads with is short by no words.
